# Every EP rank must use the same capacity: peer buffer offsets depend

experiment.control: The resolved deployed backend with its existing fixed or automatic workspace policy; retain the static fixed-workspace option as a comparator. Match R7b two DEP4 at concurrency 256/384/512 and R10 DEP8 at 1024 within each layout.
experiment.correctness: Require global capacity agreement, collective participation by idle ranks, no deadlock, bit-exact eligible outputs against the fixed path, and a verified maximum number of MegaMoE tokens entering each DSpark verification step.
experiment.cost: Read-only presence and eligibility inspection first; then targeted multi-rank correctness tests and paired eight-B200 serving runs. No GPU execution is available in this session.
experiment.held_out_condition: Unequal and zero-token rank batches under CUDA graph replay, plus a held-out arrival trace with measured cache hits and a different concurrency mix.
experiment.inconclusive_if: The active image or flags cannot be recovered, cache-hit rates or request streams differ, the path is already active without a separable control, or measurement uncertainty masks the delta.
experiment.metrics: TTFT, TPOT/ITL, throughput, separately defined custom and AIPerf strict SLO goodput, cost per token, quality, MegaMoE decode time, workspace bytes, KV capacity and occupancy, and collective hangs/errors.
experiment.rejects_if: The active path is ineligible, the token or peer-offset contract fails, correctness fails, or paired serving results show no useful net benefit after KV capacity is included.
experiment.supports_if: The path is eligible and absent from control, rank and DSpark contracts pass, and paired serving runs improve TPOT or throughput without material loss of KV capacity, goodput, cost, or quality. Any performance threshold must be chosen before testing.
experiment.treatment: Decode-sized workspace selection with a fixed-workspace fallback when any rank exceeds the common capacity.

card.mechanism: Select a smaller workspace for eligible decode batches while preserving identical peer buffer offsets across ranks; any saved active capacity may reduce MegaMoE overhead, while the additional allocation may reduce KV capacity.

card.statement: Test a decode-sized MegaMoE workspace for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on the eight-B200 node, conditional on the deployed engine selecting FlashInfer CuTeDSL MegaMoE and supporting the required workspace API. PR #62073 describes a capacity of `max_num_seqs × (1 + num_speculative_tokens)` per sequence-parallel rank, selected only when every data-parallel rank fits because peer offsets depend on shared capacity. A smaller active workspace might reduce decode address or capacity overhead, but its extra allocation and warmup could take memory from KV cache and reduce useful concurrency. No controlled DeepSeek B200 decode performance measurement appears in the inspected sources; the PR throughput measurement concerns Beam prefill on GB300. Establish backend inclusion and the actual DSpark verification token bound first, then compare full serving behavior and correctness against a fixed-workspace control. The B200 decode bottleneck and effect size are unknown.

improvement_path.rationale: Inspecting the deployed backend and workspace policy is a cheap eligibility check. A smaller decode workspace offers a testable path to lower TPOT or higher throughput, while KV capacity may offset any gain. The B200 bottleneck and effect size are unknown.

legal_correct_integration.rationale: The newer adapter says, “Every EP rank must use the same capacity,” and the proposal plans a fallback and zero-rank tests. The active backend, required API, DSpark verification token bound, and multi-rank correctness remain unverified. PR #62073 says, “The MegaMoE runtime paths still need CI or a nightly-FlashInfer machine.”

source_support.rationale: The PR author claims the workspace “is used when every DP rank's batch fits”; the supplied newer-head code independently shows a CuTeDSL workspace gate. The reported 1.71× result is for Beam prefill on GB300, not B200 decode. R1 correctly treats its B200 benefit as an inference with unknown effect size. The #57604 decode quote concerns a different staging change and does not challenge this workspace hypothesis.

controlled_experiment.rationale: R1 names the R7b and R10 concurrency points and appropriate serving, quality, and KV measurements, but omits their supplied baseline values and both required goodput definitions. It also does not explicitly freeze image digest, runtime flags, precision, and MTP/DSpark state before paired runs.

objections: The active deployment may already select the decode workspace; the historical source pin does not establish absence in the refreshed configuration.
PR #62073 reports GB300 Beam prefill results and deferred MegaMoE runtime validation; B200 decode performance and correctness are unmeasured.
The #57604 decode result concerns staging and gather changes, so it is not counterevidence to workspace selection.
The baseline comparison must retain R7b custom goodput 6.6288 and AIPerf strict goodput 4.6727 as separate measurements.
review.required_revision: Keep the eligibility-first hypothesis. Identify the newer code as PR-head evidence, verify the deployed backend and DSpark token bound, and remove the irrelevant #57604 counterevidence. Freeze the effective image, flags, precision, and MTP/DSpark state; state the supplied R7b 256/384/512 and R10 1024 baseline values and both goodput definitions before proposing paired runs.
